answer: An agent marketplace weights votes on contract rules by tokens locked for 90 days, with each token counted only once across all accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting power. Aliases may whisper or raise a gale, but they cannot widen that ledge of influence. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, bearing their price risk and losing access to that capital for the lock period.
